extracted.intended_audience: book and journal editors, copyeditors, proofreaders, indexers, production staff, and authors preparing manuscripts for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical guidance for preparing, editing, citing, and producing books and journal articles (including electronic formats), covering punctuation, citations, dates, electronic files and publications, indexing, illustrations, rights, and production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references (in text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references in text: handling alterations; formation (and see); checking and editing; use in electronic publications; use for illustrations; use with mathematical copy and enunciations; notes and citations; proofing; inclusion of specific page numbers; linking to whole chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates: formats and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats for dates (all-numeral; day–month–year; month–day–year; year–month–day ISO), avoiding ambiguity, adjectival use, punctuation, inclusive and incomplete dates, decades and centuries, fiscal years, holidays, and use in titles and various source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 6.38, 6.108, 9.35–9.40, 14.224, fig.1.9; guidance on abbreviations for months and years, alphabetizing, editorial doubt, punctuation with commas/en dashes/hyphens/slashes; contexts include access dates, interviews, manuscript collections, multimedia, patents, unpublished materials, and prefaces (see 14.x and 15.x cross-references).

rubrics_metrics.name: DOIs (Digital Object Identifiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOIs: defined and treated as persistent identifiers; use in metadata and citations; use for journal articles and electronic supplementary data; resolvers and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: include DOIs on copyright page and metadata (1.20, 1.28, 1.33, fig.1.1); recommended for journal articles (1.79, 1.82, 1.92, 1.103); guidance on DOIs vs. permalinks and URLs (14.8, 14.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publications: components and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic publications: address accessibility, authority/permanence, components (biographical notes, cross-references, front/back matter, hyperlinks, illustrations, indexes, running heads, TOC, tables), copyright issues, navigation, functional features, devices required, formats, and proofing/testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2.82n1, 3.28, 3.88, 7.49, 12.2n1. Includes advice on page markers, reflowable formats, scanned versions, searchable nature, versioning, and interplay with print elements (footnotes, fixed page numbers). Proofing/testing and metadata are emphasized (1.92, 2.137–2.140).

rubrics_metrics.name: E-books: production and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: E-books: defined as a common publishing format; include CIP data, front matter, navigation, hyperlinks, impression numbering, markup, indexing, PDF as basis, proofing and testing, and source-citation treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 1.2, 1.118–1.123; see 1.28 (ISBNs/impression), 1.119–1.121 (functional features), 1.125 and 16.13 (indexes), and 2.139/fig.2.8 on testing and proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic files: preparation and archival practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic files: archival practices, backups, cleaning up files, conversion, formats, submission to publisher, file naming and extensions, password protection, prepress proofs, page numbering, updating, and separate files for components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 1.114 for archiving; 2.4–2.8, 2.26–2.40, 2.71, 2.77, 2.80, 2.85, 2.86, 2.88, 2.107, 2.113, 2.137. Guidance includes lists of separate component files (2.26, 3.16), naming conventions for artwork (3.16), and version-control/file-hosting practices (2.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: File formats and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and use of file formats for e-books, electronic supplementary data, illustrations, multimedia content, and journal/magazine articles; interaction with hyperlinks and functional features; testing and platform considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endnotes vs. Footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Endnotes: placement (after each chapter or back matter), editing, length considerations, use with footnotes, numbering, indexing of endnotes, running heads, pros and cons, and special needs in journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 1.62, 14.43–14.59; figs.14.3–14.7; manuscript prep guidance (2.22); use in journal articles and threading with footnotes; indexer and proofing implications (16.111, 2.114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes (em and en): definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Em dashes and en dashes: definitions, lengths, marking in manuscript and proofs, keyboarding and typing, spacing and punctuation rules, uses (parenthetical elements, dialogue, lists, indexes, table cells), and non-English variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Em dashes: 6.85–6.92, marking manuscript 2.14/2.96, proofs 2.132; En dashes: 6.78–6.84, uses in ranges and compounds, spacing/punctuation issues; see also comparisons with hyphens and 3-em/2-em dashes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses: definition and safe use
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipses: defined, spacing and punctuation, danger of skewed meaning when omitting material, usage in drama/poetry/mathematics, editing and cleanup in electronic files, and when not to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 6.15, 13.50–13.58, 13.51, 13.52–13.55; non-English usages noted for French/Italian/Russian/Spanish; guidance on combining with brackets, colons, exclamation points, and periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial interpolations, clarifications, and permissible changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial interpolations and clarifications: permissible changes to quoted/referenced materials, handling missing or illegible words, use of sic, punctuation choices, and editorial doubt with respect to errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 13.59–13.63, 13.7, 6.68, 14.132, 15.34, 15.44. Guidance addresses how to mark or correct original quotations, use of brackets/notes, and avoiding unnecessary alteration of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair-use doctrine guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair-use doctrine: legal overview, Chicago's guidelines, rules of thumb, relationship to attribution, interplay with Creative Commons licenses, applicability to dissertations/theses and various materials (charts, tables, epigraphs, illustrations, interviews, paraphrasing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.84–4.94, 4.86–4.87, 4.93, 1.84, and material-specific notes (charts/tables 4.91, epigraphs 4.87, illustrations 4.90, unpublished works 4.88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic rights, enhanced rights, and DRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic rights and enhanced electronic rights: negotiation, relation to DRM, copyright page metadata, and publisher/author agreements concerning distribution and subsidiary rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.63–4.66, 4.34, 4.51, 4.52; DRM/DRM discussion pp.978–979; guidance on licensing for derivative uses and distribution rights (4.13, 4.34, 4.64, 4.76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata and error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling errors: errata pages for books and journals, checking and correcting errors in text and grammar, responsibility for corrections, proofing/prepress procedures, and silent correction practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See entries on errata (1.68, 1.90, 1.94, 1.112), errors in grammar/punctuation (5.x, 6.x), checking and correction workflows (2.56, 2.69–2.70, 2.107, 2.137–2.138), and indexer notation of errors (16.125, 16.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic workflow and markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic workflow: checklists for production, use of formal markup languages and DTDs, metadata practices, and proofing/testing as part of the electronic workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2.139, 1.117, 2.83, 2.137, 1.92, fig.2.8. Emphasizes regression testing, feature definition documents, and integration of markup with production checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' responsibilities and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors: manuscript-preparation guidelines, responsibility for bias-free language, ownership and copyright issues for editors' contributions, biographical notes and credits, and roles for journals and multiauthor volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See entries on editors and editors' names (1.64, 1.84–1.89, 2.41–2.42, 4.57–4.59, 14.103–14.104); includes guidance on forewords, prefaces, proofing, and omission/abbreviation conventions in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming and version control
rubrics_metrics.description: File names: conventions for artwork and production files, use of extensions, typographic considerations, production checklist inclusion, and version-control/file-hosting recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 3.16, 2.37, 7.77–7.79, 2.77, 2.78, 2.103; guidance on slashes in filenames and naming formats for submission to publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts and typefaces: selection and embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: Fonts and typefaces: guidance on use for computer terminology, embedding fonts in digital artwork, archaic fonts, and interaction with electronic file cleanup and conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See pp.980, 989 and entries on embedded fonts and digital artwork (3.15, 12.13, 2.80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and illustrations: preparation and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures: definition and use of figures, source citation formats, text references, separate electronic files for artwork, and preparation guidelines for prints vs. scans and digital artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 3.1–3.16, 3.43, 3.86, 3.15–3.20, 14.150–14.158; guidance includes numbering, callouts, file formats, and submission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and indexer workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing: deadlines and scheduling, double posting, indexer’s notation of errors, indexing of first lines and proper names, embedded index use in electronic publications, and proofing/editing indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 16.x entries (16.4, 16.7, 16.13, 16.32, 16.71, 16.84, 16.99, 16.101–16.145), plus production checklist and electronic submission (2.2, 2.77, 16.102–16.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical expressions and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of mathematical expressions: delimiters, enclosures, elided elements, exponents, decimals, special symbols, transcription formatting, and alignment in tables and graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See chapter 12 references (12.13–12.66, 12.19–12.20, 12.26–12.56, 12.60); includes guidance on display expressions, Dirac notation, determinants, vertical bars, and alignment in tables/graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation style and common punctuation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation: rules and exceptions for commas, colons, semicolons, parentheses, quotation marks, hyphens, slashes, periods, exclamation points, question marks, spacing rules (en/em/word spaces), and punctuation in non-English contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See many cross-references across chapters 6, 7, 11–13; includes language-specific notes, interaction with quotation and dialogue formatting, and proofing marks for manuscript & proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiformat publishing (print + electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing in multiple formats: treatment of identifiers, citations, page numbering, navigation/TOC, functional features, and the relationships between print and electronic elements (what print elements may be absent in electronic versions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 1.26, 1.77–1.83, 14.16, 14.22, 14.47, 14.160–14.174; guidance on impression numbering, page markers in EPUB, prepress issues, and how to cite different versions.
